subject: Harmonia: exec signoff needed — indemnity & warranty concession request
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Baxter <sofia@harmonia.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Harmonia: initial ask — indemnity & warranty concessions (SOW v3 attached)

Sofia / Karthik / Ben —

Thanks again for the productive conversation yesterday. Attached is the SOW v3 that reflects product scope and delivery timeline. Harmonia came back this morning with two contract asks that push well outside our standard risk profile:

- Remove/limit Redwood's liability cap (their redline removes the $250k cap and proposes a pro rata revenue-based cap tied to annual recurring revenue).
- Expand indemnity to include third-party claims even where Redwood's fault is not established; they're also asking for a 10-year survival on indemnities.
- Narrow our warranty disclaimer and add a customer remedy of credit + service remediation (they specifically asked for a 90-day service warranty window).

They have also requested a 45% discount on list pricing for the first 12 months to fund a joint pilot. The commercial team thinks the ARR uplift is strong but legal flagged material exposure.

Attached: Harmonia_SOW_v3.pdf and their requested_redlines (Harmonia_requested_redlines.docx). I'm looping legal (Karthik) and Sales Ops (Ben). Jonas — would appreciate your read if we decide this is strategic and worth executive approval for a exceptions package.

Ask: Karthik, can you confirm that these redlines require explicit exec sign-off? If so, please summarize recommended guardrails and an approval path. Ben, I'll need the margin impact and churn risk if we accept 45% first-year discount.

Next steps: If execs are open, I'll ask Harmonia to sign a mutual confidentiality amendment and a short-term guardrail amendment (e.g., incident liability carveouts) while we work the final SOW.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Harmonia: initial ask — indemnity & warranty concessions (SOW v3 attached)

Marissa —

Thanks for the context and the redline. Quick read: this is a high-risk request and yes, it needs executive sign-off. Key concerns and suggested negotiation positions below.

1) Liability cap removal: unacceptable as written. If the business case is strong, recommend adjusting to a higher fixed cap tied to committed ARR tiers rather than removing it entirely. Example: 
   - For ARR < $1M, cap = $250k
   - For ARR $1M–$5M, cap = $500k
   - >$5M, cap = $1M (with board/CFO notice)

2) Indemnity expansion: they want to broaden indemnitees and extend survival to 10 years. We should insist on limiting indemnity to third-party IP claims and claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct. Ten-year survival is excessive — propose 3 years for indemnities.

3) Warranty language: the customer wants a service-level warranty with credit remedies. We can accept a limited service warranty tied to uptime targets (SLA) and remedial service credits capped at a multiple of monthly fees (e.g., up to 3x monthly fees for repetitive failures) — but not monetary makewhole beyond the liability cap.

4) Discount: 45% first-year is aggressive. If this is strategic (pilot-to-deal motion) we can consider a performance-linked structure: 30% upfront discount if renewal ARR >= target in 12 months, otherwise revert to 15% discount. 

5) Insurance and risk mitigation: require cyber liability insurance (min $5M) and explicit incident reporting timelines. Also suggest a mutual termination right and data return/secure delete clause.

Given these adjustments, I recommend we escalate to Jonas for approval of exception parameters (discount + cap ladder + indemnity survival). If Jonas approves, Legal will draft an exception memo for Red team records and prepare an addendum.

I'll attach a marked-up excerpt of the indemnity and cap clauses to use in the exec memo.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Harmonia: initial ask — indemnity & warranty concessions (SOW v3 attached)

Marissa / Karthik —

Quick commercial color: Harmonias' CFO confirmed 12-month pilot ARR = $1.2M if we close. They view the 45% as necessary to move procurement this quarter. Margin impact for Year 1 at 45% is significant — I attached a simple model. Highlights:

- Year 1 net revenue at 45% discount: ~$660k
- Year 2 expected renewal (conservative) 70% at list pricing with 15% retention discount (if pilot is successful)
- Lifetime value assumptions look okay but cashflow negative in first year.

If execs demand a higher cap (Karthik's ladder proposal) + 30% conditional discount tied to pilot KPIs, I can make the number work with Product committing to a focused implementation calweek to secure success.

We should also ask for a short-term collateral: mutual data processing addendum (DPA) and a holdback of 20% of the first invoice until pilot acceptance. That reduces financial exposure while giving the customer time to prove value.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Harmonia: initial ask — indemnity & warranty concessions (SOW v3 attached)

Team —

Thank you for laying this out. I took a pass with the commercial and legal guidance in mind. My decision: approve an exceptions package, with strict conditions. Summarizing the guardrails I am willing to approve now: 

1) Discount: Approve up to 30% first-year discount, contingent on the pilot KPIs we define in the SOW and a written renewal commitment (minimum 12 months at no more than 15% renewal discount). Any higher discount requires CFO sign-off.

2) Liability cap: Approve a tiered cap ladder as Karthik proposed but slightly tightened:
   - ARR < $1M cap = $250k
   - ARR $1M–$3M cap = $500k
   - ARR > $3M cap = $1M (requires CFO and GC concurrence)

3) Indemnity & survival: Do not expand indemnity beyond IP infringement and third-party bodily injury claims tied to Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct. Limit survival to three years. No open-ended indemnity.

4) Warranty & remedies: Accept a limited service warranty tied to SLA targets; credits capped at 3x monthly fees and never exceeding the liability cap. No separate monetary remedies outside the cap.

5) Risk controls: Require proof of $5M cyber insurance, incident reporting timelines, a DPA signed before first data transfer, and a 20% payment holdback until pilot acceptance.

6) Exec memo & audit trail: Legal to prepare an exception memo capturing the rationale, financial tradeoffs, and an explicit owner for the renewal commitment. Sales to secure a signed addendum from Harmonia accepting these guardrails before any invoice.

Marissa — proceed with the conditional offer (30% + guardrails). Karthik, please prepare the exception memo and the limited addendum reflecting the approved guardrails. Ben — reflect the approved 30% scenario in the deal finance and include the holdback schedule.

I'll sign the exception memo once it's ready. This is approved at the CEO level limited to the conditions above. Any deviation requires CFO sign-off.

Jonas Weber
Chief Executive Officer
Redwood Inference
